Weeks ago, JPMorgan set a price target of US$345 for Apple stock with a December 2027 horizon. After yesterday's quarterly results, the investment bank has slightly lowered its outlook. Here are the details.

JPMorgan Lowers Apple Price Target

According to AppleInsider, JPMorgan has lowered its price target on Apple stock from US$345 to US$340.

AppleInsider reports:

JPMorgan's adjustment comes after Apple released its quarterly results yesterday and warned that memory shortages would significantly worsen supply constraints in the September quarter, with the iPhone, iPad and Mac being the most affected. These three segments typically account for roughly 64% of Apple's revenue in its fourth fiscal quarter.

In yesterday's report, Apple also disclosed a 5% decline in iPad revenue and discussed slowing growth in its services business, citing in part weaker App Store gaming revenue, regulatory changes in some countries, and the ongoing dispute with Epic Games, which prevents Apple from collecting commissions on transactions completed via external links in the United States.

Apple's stock opened down 8.6% today, currently trading at US$301.41, a 9.6% drop from the previous close. The market reaction is intense, coming just days after Apple briefly surpassed a US$5 trillion market capitalisation, overtaking Nvidia to become the world's most valuable company. Apple is still up 11% year-to-date.

To read the AppleInsider report, click here.

Update, 3:46 p.m. ET: AppleInsider also noted that Morgan Stanley lowered its price target on Apple stock from US$364 to US$360, while Goldman Sachs cut its target from US$370 to US$360.
